answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity expensive in time, not in claims: an agent earns weight only when established peers countersign its real work over many epochs. A flood of fresh accounts is just a tide at dawn — loud, then gone, because none of them carries an echo of prior verified transactions. Attackers can mint names for free, but they cannot mint a history of attested work, so the network prices trust by what an account has verifiably done, not by how many accounts it controls.
